package_info.package_manager: N/A (exploits Atlassian Confluence via CVE-2023-22527, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.package_versions: Confluence Data Center and Server (affected versions prior to January 2024 patch)
package_info.why_malicious: The Godzilla backdoor is a fileless, in-memory malware that exploits a critical template injection vulnerability (CVE-2023-22527) in Atlassian Confluence. It enables unauthenticated remote code execution, persistent in-memory webshell access, and AES-encrypted C2 communication, all while evading traditional file-based detection.

execution_context.trigger: HTTP POST request to vulnerable template endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon receiving an HTTP POST request to the vulnerable template endpoint, the server evaluates attacker-supplied OGNL/JavaScript code via template injection, which decodes and loads a Base64-encoded Java class into JVM memory, resulting in arbitrary code execution and in-memory payload deployment.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of template injection to execute attacker-controlled OGNL/JavaScript code, especially with dynamic class loading from Base64 payloads, is a direct exploitation technique for remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Templates are expected to render static or sanitized data, not execute arbitrary code or load classes based on user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There is no legitimate use for user-supplied code execution or class loading in this context; template engines should never evaluate unsanitized user input.
key_indicators: OGNL/JavaScript code injection in HTTP POST requests
Base64-encoded Java class payloads embedded in parameters
Use of ScriptEngineManager for dynamic code execution

execution_context.trigger: In-memory class loading after template injection

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After in-memory class loading via template injection, the injected Java class uses reflection to access private fields and Tomcat internals, then injects a custom Valve into the Tomcat pipeline, establishing a persistent in-memory webshell for ongoing attacker access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Reflection is used to bypass normal Java access controls and manipulate Tomcat's internal structures, which is highly abnormal and enables deep compromise of the server.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Application code should not access or modify servlet container internals or inject runtime webshells using reflection.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Reflection is used in frameworks for dependency injection or serialization, but not for arbitrary field access or runtime webshell injection.
key_indicators: Reflection to access and modify private fields
Injection of custom Valve into Tomcat pipeline at runtime
Dynamic class loading and manipulation of servlet container

execution_context.trigger: Webshell command execution via HTTP requests

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the in-memory webshell receives an HTTP request, it decrypts the AES-encrypted command from the request, executes the command on the server, encrypts the output, and returns the encrypted result to the attacker, enabling covert remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: AES-encrypted command-and-control over HTTP is a strong indicator of a backdoor, as it conceals attacker activity and facilitates remote code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Servlet Valves should not process arbitrary encrypted commands or execute system commands received via HTTP requests.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption is used for legitimate API traffic, but not for executing system commands or establishing covert C2 channels.
key_indicators: Command execution via decrypted HTTP parameters

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a malicious HTTP POST exploiting CVE-2023-22527 to inject OGNL/JavaScript code and a Base64-encoded payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: In-memory loading and execution of the Godzilla webshell class.

attack_chain.action: Injected code decodes and loads the MemGodValueShell class into JVM memory using reflection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Injection of a custom Valve into the Tomcat pipeline.

attack_chain.action: Custom Valve (GodzillaValue) is activated, establishing a persistent in-memory webshell.
attack_chain.leads_to: Server is now backdoored and awaits attacker commands.

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends AES-encrypted commands via HTTP to the webshell, which decrypts, executes, and returns encrypted results.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full remote control of the server and exfiltration of results.

behavioral_signatures: Template injection leading to dynamic class loading and code execution
Reflection-based access and modification of Tomcat internals
Injection of custom Valve objects into the Tomcat pipeline at runtime
AES-encrypted command-and-control traffic over HTTP to Confluence endpoints
file_indicators: No persistent files (fileless); presence of suspicious in-memory Valve objects
Unusual classes loaded in JVM memory (e.g., MemGodValueShell, GodzillaValue)
Absence of corresponding class files on disk despite active webshell behavior
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests to /template/aui/text-inline.vm containing OGNL/JavaScript payloads
AES-encrypted HTTP traffic to Confluence endpoints, especially with 'cmd' parameters
Unusual HTTP traffic patterns to Confluence from external sources
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for template injection attempts and OGNL/JavaScript code in HTTP POST requests to Confluence endpoints. Detect in-memory anomalies such as unexpected Valve objects or classes loaded via reflection. Analyze HTTP traffic for AES-encrypted command patterns and suspicious parameters (e.g., 'cmd') in requests to Confluence. Use memory forensics to identify webshells that do not exist on disk. Correlate with known C2 patterns for Godzilla and similar backdoors, and alert on the presence of in-memory classes like MemGodValueShell or GodzillaValue.
